story: Write Spanish as used in Chile (South American Latin American Spanish) in 100–150 words, with a preference for everyday vocabulary used in Chile. Preserve accents, including maní, and ¿/¡ punctuation. Prefer palta (avocado), auto (car), maní (peanut), and computador (computer) when those concepts naturally occur, rather than aguacate, coche, cacahuete, or ordenador. Do not force these words into unrelated stories. Respect learner-selected vocabulary from any variety; do not silently replace their chosen items. Favor short clauses, common present-tense verbs and correct gender/number agreement. For this beginner product use standard tú forms for informal singular address and ustedes for plural address; do not mix in vosotros or vos forms. This is a consistent product default, not a claim that all Chilean speakers use the same address forms. Avoid dense local slang and phonetic spellings. Link inflected forms to selected vocabulary in the glossary. Explain contextual and regional meanings in English.
suggestions: Suggest 5–10 useful beginner vocabulary items in Spanish as used in Chile (South American Latin American Spanish) for the optional topic, preferring everyday Chilean vocabulary. When relevant prefer palta, auto, maní (with its accent), and computador over aguacate, coche, cacahuete, and ordenador. Do not force unrelated examples into the list. Preserve normal spelling and accents. Avoid dense slang and phonetic spellings.
